title: Graph: producer surplus, Grab as monopoly vs competition
scenario: Grab faces P = 339 − Q with MC = 147 THB. The monopoly equilibrium is Q = 96 at P = 243; the competitive equilibrium is Q = 192 at P = 147. This graph labels its areas differently from the consumer-surplus graph: A, B, C and D as drawn.

questions.stem: On this graph, which area is producer surplus in the competitive (Bertrand) equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Under Bertrand P = MC = 147, so no unit sells above its marginal cost and producer surplus is zero.

questions.stem: On this graph, which area is producer surplus in the monopoly equilibrium?
questions.explanation: B is the rectangle between the monopoly price (243) and MC (147) over 96 rides: (243 − 147) × 96 = 9,216. D is the cost of producing those rides.

questions.stem: On this graph, what does area D represent?
choices: The total cost of producing the monopoly output, MC × Q
questions.explanation: D is the rectangle under MC = 147 from 0 to 96: 147 × 96 = 14,112, the cost of producing those rides.

questions.stem: On this graph, which area is lost to everyone under monopoly?
questions.explanation: C is the triangle between demand and MC from 96 to 192. On this graph the letters differ from the consumer-surplus graph, where the same triangle is B.

choices: What producers receive by selling each unit at a price above its marginal cost
What consumers save below their willingness to pay
questions.explanation: Price minus marginal cost, summed over units sold.
